compiled:
📰 General

NBA’s Final Regular Season Games Determine Playoff Seeds and Potential Matchups •

With 15 games scheduled for Sunday, the final day of the 2025-26 NBA regular season will determine the seeding for all 30 teams. Several key matchups will impact playoff positioning, including contests involving teams vying for the final eight spots. The Boston Celtics and Milwaukee Bucks are currently battling for the Eastern Conference’s top seed, while the Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers are competing for the Western Conference crown. Teams like the Phoenix Suns and Sacramento Kings are also in contention for playoff berths.

🌍 World

Nigerian Military Strike Kills Civilians at Borno Market – Reports Indicate Casualties •

A Nigerian military air strike has resulted in the feared deaths of civilians at a market in the Borno state region. The attack occurred near the border with Yobe state, according to initial reports. Witnesses claim Nigerian military jets were engaged in an operation at the time of the strike. The exact number of casualties remains unconfirmed, with local sources expressing concerns about the impact on the community. Investigations into the incident are currently underway.

🦅 US

“Euphoria” Season 3 Signals a Shift as Series Evolves Beyond Its Initial Impact •

The third season of “Euphoria” marks a significant departure from the series’ beginnings, reflecting a change in its audience and narrative scope. The show’s initial success in 2019 centered around the rising stars Sydney Sweeney and Jacob Elordi, alongside Zendaya’s transition into a darker role. Season three explores more complex themes and character arcs, moving beyond the series’ early focus on teenage drama and relationships. Production has reportedly shifted to a more mature and ambitious approach, incorporating higher production values and a broader range of storylines.

💰 Business

Ford Rebrands Campus Streets, Removing Carroll Shelby’s Legacy Name •

Ford Motor Company is renaming several streets surrounding its new headquarters campus in Dearborn, Michigan. The company is removing the names of streets previously dedicated to Carroll Shelby, the iconic race car designer and Ford’s most famous collaboration. This renaming initiative is part of a broader campus redevelopment project undertaken by Ford. The move reflects a strategic shift away from Shelby’s association with the company’s performance vehicles. The new street names are yet to be officially announced.

💻 Technology

Arc Raiders Introduces New Map Conditions Tracker for Strategic Gameplay •

Embark Studios has launched a new map conditions tracker accessible on the Arc Raiders website. The tracker displays the current state of environmental hazards across the game’s map. It forecasts upcoming conditions, allowing players to anticipate and prepare for shifting threats like firestorms and ice storms. This tool provides data on the intensity and projected movement of these dynamic hazards. Players can utilize this information to optimize their strategies and improve their chances of success.

🎭 Entertainment

Asha Bhosle, Iconic Bollywood Singer, Passes Away at 92 •

Asha Bhosle, a globally renowned singer and one of India’s most prolific recording artists, died in Mumbai on Sunday at the age of 92. Her son, Anand Bhosle, announced her passing. Bhosle’s career spanned over seven decades, marked by her exceptional vocal range and significant contributions to Bollywood music. She holds the record for the most recorded voices in modern Indian music, having released thousands of songs across various genres.

🏅 Sports

Louisville Baseball Sees Success with Kelsey and Oregon Signee Shelstad •

Louisville Cardinals baseball head coach Pat Kelsey hosted Oregon signee, Riley Shelstad, at Saturday’s game, creating a significant recruiting opportunity. The event allowed Kelsey to personally connect with a highly-regarded prospect and showcase the program. Shelstad, a promising pitcher, attended the game alongside Kelsey, solidifying her commitment to the Cardinals. This dual-player visit highlights Louisville’s proactive approach to recruiting top talent.

🔬 Science

Public Support for Space Exploration Remains Strong, New Poll Reveals •

A recent Ipsos poll following the Artemis II launch indicates continued high public support for NASA’s space exploration endeavors. Sixty-two percent of US adults believe the benefits of sending humans into space outweigh the associated costs. This sentiment aligns closely with previous polling data over the past 80 years, demonstrating a consistent level of public interest. The poll highlights a significant portion of the population’s belief in the value of space exploration.

🩺 Health

Edna Foa, Pioneer of Exposure Therapy for PTSD, Passes Away at 88 •

Edna Foa, a prominent Israeli-American psychologist, passed away on March 24th at the age of 88. She is credited with significantly advancing the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) through her advocacy for direct exposure therapy. Foa’s work focused on helping patients confront their fears and anxieties directly, rather than relying solely on avoidance techniques. Her innovations have become a cornerstone of PTSD treatment protocols globally, impacting countless individuals seeking recovery.
